newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends lower as soybeans and corn fall.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends lower as soybeans and corn fall.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed mostly lower, pulled down by a drop in soybean and corn futures, traders said.
Corn and beans were hit by bearishly-construed crop production estimates in the Clinton budget for 1998.

The fiscal 1998 budget proposed for the Agriculture Department pegged 1997 U.S. wheat production at 2.345 billion bushels of wheat. Early this week, the U.S. Feed Grains Council said 1997 U.S. wheat production would total 2.449 billion bushels. March wheat was buoyed early by export news.
"There was wheat business overnight and maybe some Iraqi business," a trader said.

Also, traders cited reports Egypt overnight bought 110,000 tonnes of U.S. or Australian wheat and may be tendering for more. Also there was talk Iraq was in the market for 50,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat.

Technical support in March wheat was noted early as wheat recently fell to contract lows and was oversold according to technical indicators. The nine day relative strength index (RSI) for the March closed at 27-1/2 percent.
Wheat closed four cents a bushel lower to 1/2 cent higher, with March down 3-1/2 at $3.58.
The market generally considers an RSI of 30 or less as an oversold market.
July was pressured by an improved crop outlook. "New crop was under pressure because of the moisture coming in (U.S. Plains)," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
Local selling led the declines in wheat late with Refco Inc and Griffin Trading also noted sellers of one million bushels each of the March contract.
Cargill Inc was an early buyer of 1.5 million bushels of March but when that demand waned wheat futures began their downward spiral.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 14,000 contracts, above 12,810 contracts traded Wednesday, CBOT reported.
Activity in wheat options also suggested a further bearish tone in put volatility.
"They're still selling the July premium so the put volatility should come down in the next few days," an options trader said.

FIMAT Futures bought 750 March $3.90 puts and sold 750 March $3.10 calls, Refco Inc bought 400 March $3.90 calls at 3/4 cent and Goldenberg Hehmeyer sold 400 July $3.60 calls at 11 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated by the CBOT at 4,000 contracts, above the 3,000 traded Wednesday.
